part.text: Confirmed: those date failures are pre-existing environment issues (locale/timezone), identical before and after my change. Quick sanity check of the fix:

The fix works. Summary:

- **gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriter.java:715** — changed the check in `value(double)` from an unconditional throw to `if (!lenient && (Double.isNaN(value) || Double.isInfinite(value)))`, matching the behavior of `value(Number)`. In lenient mode, `Double.toString` already emits the canonical `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` literals, so they now stream without boxing.
- Updated the `value(double)` javadoc to document that NaN/infinities are allowed in lenient mode.

Verified: `JsonWriterTest` (39/39), full `JsonReader`/`JsonWriter` streaming suites, and a manual check showing `[NaN,Infinity,-Infinity,1.5]` in lenient mode and an exception in strict mode. The only remaining test failures are pre-existing date/locale tests that fail identically without my change.
